text: The core motivation for photonic network-on-chip is bandwidth density. A 500x220 nm silicon waveguide carrying 64 WDM channels x 100 Gbps reaches ~2 Tbps/um, versus ~20 Gbps/um for a differential electrical pair. This is roughly a:
explanation: About 2 Tbps/um versus 20 Gbps/um is a ~100x bandwidth-density advantage, and it comes from WDM multiplexing many wavelengths in one waveguide. 2x and 10x understate it, and the advantage is real and robust, unlike the 'no advantage' option.
